decisions.reason: The black-finish range costs little to hold and still has design-trend upside, but it no longer appeared on the website in 2024, which weakens the evidence and raises the risk of it being phased out.
A seamless-covering shower channel fits barrier-free bathroom architecture and the core offer at low holding cost, so the option is worth keeping despite less visibility in 2024.
The pump-assisted solution is costlier to support and may be superseded by the 2024 pump-drain channel, but its renovation potential is still uncertain enough that the option stays open for now.
A tileable floor drain is a natural, low-cost extension of the established range for installers, so holding it costs little.
The stainless steel design grate uses the firm's own manufacturing and design strengths at low marginal cost, so keeping it remains worthwhile.
Newly launched and presented on its own page, the pump-drain channel's value is still highly uncertain after only one year, so the option should clearly be kept open.
